get.description:
Whether every selected nozzle is zeroed, and which of the profile's
nozzles are.

post.description:
Zero one of the selected nozzles where it is. X/Y are set at the first
(leftmost) selected nozzle, over the print's start point; each nozzle's
height with that nozzle lowered onto the bed (about 0.2 mm above the
surface). Printess 1.0:

- `nozzles: ["left"]`, `nozzle: "left"` → G92 X0 Y0 Z0 B0
- `nozzles: ["right"]`, `nozzle: "right"` → G92 X0 Y0 A0 C0 (right nozzle
  over the start point and on the bed)
- `nozzles: ["left", "right"]`, two steps: `nozzle: "left"` → G92 X0 Y0
  Z0 B0, then lower the right nozzle onto the bed and `nozzle: "right"`
  → G92 A0 C0

Prints aren't shifted by the nozzle offsets: each nozzle prints in place.
Only the second nozzle's sections of a two-material 3MF printed with two
nozzles are shifted by its offset.
Mark calibration as invalid (e.g. after a disconnect or power cycle).

get.description: Return the most recent serial log entries.

The loaded print's processed G-code, one line per line, as sent to
the printer (before flow scaling). Its ETag is the program id, which
changes on every load and edit.

304.description: Unchanged since the ETag in If-None-Match

put.description:
Replace the loaded print's lines with the request body (text/plain,
one G-code line per line, as GET /gcode/loaded sends them).

The edit is validated, simulated and checked against the bed limits and
the syringe travel; if it fails, nothing changes and the 422 body says
which line. With If-Match, it is only applied to that program.

409.description: A print is printing or paused

412.description: If-Match names a program that is no longer loaded

get.description: Recent print sessions, newest first, with their extrusion events.

The latest reading, target and status of every sensor. `state` says
whether the printer is connected and has reported any sensor at all.
Readings for the chart: the last `minutes`, or all of one print session's.

Logged readings of one print session, or between `from` and `to`
(ISO 8601; UTC unless an offset is given), as CSV: timestamp, sensor,
name, actual, target.

post.description:
Set a heater's target with M104 (T, T<n>), M140 (B) or M141 (C); with
the lab firmware (protocol "printess"), a channel's (I<n>) with
M104 I<n> T<°C> H to heat or C to cool, chosen from its current reading
(refused without one). Allowed while printing.

Send M105 once (5 s to answer) and return the raw reply, or null if
none came, with the sensors found in it. Works with temperature control
on or off: this is how to check the printer's sensor setup.
Start temperature monitoring again after M105 polling paused.

put.description:
Save the settings; they apply at once and are kept across restarts.
Turning temperature_sensors on or off starts or stops temperature
monitoring right away, connected or not.

put.description:
Select another printer profile, until the backend restarts
(config.json's printer_profile is the one it starts with). Resets the
calibration and any resume checkpoint, and unloads the loaded print.
Refused during a print.

get.description: Every printer profile: built in, or added in config.json.

BedLimits.description:
Where the nozzles may go, in mm relative to the G92 zero point. Every
nozzle's height axis has the z range.

The printer has no homing or endstops, so these are enforced by the host
only. The defaults match the 60 × 60 × 60 mm Cura machine definition with
the zero in the middle of the bed and Z0 at the print surface. Given as
min/max rather than a size so an off-centre zero can be described.
BedLimits.title: BedLimits

BuildVolume.description:
The slicer's machine size in mm (Cura's machine_width, machine_depth
and machine_height). A model larger than this is refused before slicing.
BuildVolume.title: BuildVolume
